[← Logistics](logistics.qmd)

Working list, last checked **November 11, 2026**. Amounts and deadlines come from web searches and some come from third-party listings. Confirm each one on the funder's own page before applying. Dates marked *est.* are guesses from past cycles.

## Notes

- **Simons Travel Support for Mathematicians.** This is the best fit for regular travel and collaboration. Applicants need a tenure-track or tenured position in a mathematics department, an active publication record, and no other external grant as PI or co-PI that runs past September 1, 2027. The FAQ addresses whether statistics counts, but I couldn't confirm its answer. Check it before applying. Starting this cycle the money is paid as a grant rather than a gift, so it goes through the Bowdoin Grants Office. Decisions are expected August 1, 2027.
- **APSA.** These awards have a modest cap but suit precinct-level and local-politics work. The spring deadline has moved between March 15 and May 15 in recent years.
- **Bowdoin.** The FDC won't pay mileage to sites within 50 miles of campus. The conference travel application asks you to list FDC awards from the past six years.

## Watching, nothing open now

- **Russell Sage Foundation, Sheldon Danziger Pipeline Grants.** Grants run about $35,000–50,000, larger than a small grant. The October 21, 2026 deadline has passed; the next cycle should come around fall 2027.
- **Spencer Foundation, Small Research Grants on Education.** Grants go up to $50,000. A secondary report says Spencer is pausing new competitions in the first half of 2027 and expects to announce a redesign in June 2027.
- **MIT Election Data and Science Lab.** Its recent calls ran $25,000–100,000 on set topics, most recently voter list maintenance. No call is open now, but it's worth watching given the precinct work.
- **PIMS–BIRS Team Up!** This funds two-week team residencies in Banff or Kelowna for groups affected by obstacles to research. The 2026–27 round is closed.
- **ASA.** Travel awards go almost entirely to students and early-career members (the Student and Early Career Travel Fund and section awards). I found no faculty small-grant program.
